stages.title: The quiz form: its panels and buttons

screens.title: Make the quiz form with its six panels and their controls
screens.goal: This part makes the quiz form. It has one panel for the score and one for each question.

open.what: Each panel is filled with its own controls: labels, boxes, buttons and a list.
open.does: When it works, frmQuiz shows six panels in the Design tab. Every control has its name.

screens.title: Add the quiz form and its six panels
screens.done: frmQuiz is in Solution Explorer with six panels on it
screens.goal: I add a form called frmQuiz and put six panels on it.

blocks.p: The quiz is a form of its own, with a score panel and five question panels.

steps.do: Click the Project menu along the top. Click the line that starts Add Form.
steps.see: A box opens with Form picked in its list.
wrong: Click your project's name in Solution Explorer first. Then open the Project menu again.

steps.do: In the Name box at the bottom, type frmQuiz.cs. Click Add.
steps.see: frmQuiz opens in the Design tab. It is empty.

steps.do: Drag six panels from the Toolbox onto it. The next screen shows what to name them.
steps.see: Six panels sit on the form, waiting for their names.

screens.title: Make the Take quiz button open the quiz
screens.goal: This part gives the Take quiz button three lines of code. They close one form and open the other.

open.what: The data entry form closes, so its details must already be in Global.cs. Then the quiz form opens.
open.does: When it works, pressing Take quiz closes the data entry form. The quiz appears in its place.

screens.title: Meet the two new things for Take quiz

screens.goal: I meet the two new things the Take quiz button uses.

blocks.p: The Take quiz button sits on the data entry form and swaps it for the quiz.

code.title: The Take quiz button

partLines: Visual Studio wrote these two lines

blocks.p: [[this.Close()|0]] closes the data entry form. [[new frmQuiz().Show()|1]] makes the quiz and shows it.

blocks.watch: The data entry form forgets everything when it closes. So its details are kept in Global.cs.

screens.title: Make question 1's Check button mark a typed answer
screens.goal: This part marks question 1. The typed answer is compared with the right one in small letters.

open.what: A match adds a point and turns the panel green. Anything else turns it red.
open.does: When it works, question 1 goes green or red. Then question 2 switches on.

screens.title: Open the code behind question 1's Check button
screens.done: the code tab is open at btnCheck1_Click with your cursor between its curly brackets
screens.goal: I open the code behind question 1's Check button and meet .ToLower() and BackColor.

blocks.p: Question 1 is typed in a box, and its Check button marks it.
[[.ToLower()|2]] turns every letter small. So EMERGENCY and Emergency both match.
[[BackColor|3]] is the background colour of a panel. Green means right. Red means wrong.

steps.do: Open frmQuiz in the Design tab. Double-click the Check button of question 1.
steps.see: The code tab opens at btnCheck1_Click.
